findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the max_width/max_height version
findings.body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is still present. In Ruby the later definition overwrites the earlier one, so the 5-argument form (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) now raises ArgumentError. Any existing caller using that signature breaks. Only one of the two signatures should remain, or the callers should be updated and the old one removed.

findings.title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle --resize-fit
findings.body: The controller calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`. For animated GIFs (when allow_animated_thumbnails is on), `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which emits `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects a WxH geometry, not a percentage, so the command will fail. `convert_with` then returns false silently, and the oversized GIF is uploaded anyway.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and oversized images are uploaded silently
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure (convert_with swallows errors and returns false), but the return value is ignored. The loop runs at most 5 times and then falls through to `Upload.create_for` regardless of whether the file is still above max_image_size_kb. The user gets no error, and an image that exceeds the configured limit is stored. The loop should stop on a failed conversion and reject or report the upload if the file is still too large.

findings.title: Remote URL download limit no longer follows the max_image_size_kb setting
findings.body: The download size cap was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Admins who lower the setting will now have URL uploads accepted up to 10MB, and the setting is no longer enforced for this path. The image-downsizing change does not require this change to the cap, so the regression is unnecessary.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores the per-type site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now hardcodes 10MB for every upload type, so `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` are no longer respected by the client. Admin limits are bypassed in the UI, and attachments can be accepted up to 10MB even when the site caps them lower. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoding problem.

findings.title: 413 error message hardcodes 10 MB instead of the configured limit
findings.body: The 413 branch now reports a fixed 10 MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The displayed limit can be wrong for any site that has configured a different value, so the user is told the wrong maximum.

findings.title: Commit/PR description is a placeholder
findings.body: The PR description is just "Test 1" and does not explain the new behavior, the setting interaction, or the hardcoded 10MB change. A maintainer cannot review the intent or the regression risks from it.
